evidence_layer_rule: Provenance layer and lifecycle status are separate dimensions. Multi-source practice never overrides official_current, and a transient page or button observation never proves business completion.

official_sources.boundary: The 11 site/entity/currency groups are contract routing evidence only; registration, granular country authorization and store activation remain unproven.
The USD 5m statement conflicts with the current signup form's Under $2M range; leave eligibility threshold unknown and do not generalize US onboarding.
CHOICE is a performance label, not a mode/tier/ad. Preserve the low-stock anomaly without inventory action; paid ads remain unconnected and not globally disproved.
Unique warehouse and duplicate-fulfillment prevention are rules; no app authorization, warehouse mapping or fulfillment write is proven.
Public screening fields and exemption text do not prove submission, approval, KYC, site/category/brand authorization, store activation or a minimum revenue threshold.
Marketing category families, fixed-fee wording and $0 benefit labels do not prove category schema/authorization, fee rates, paid-ad account/API, billing identity or campaign eligibility.
Public must-haves are not the authenticated category schema.
Recommendations and examples are not universal hard limits.
Documented solutions do not prove app review, scope or connection.
Mode-specific fields may be null and must be inspected at runtime.
Requirements differ by store/category; query before drafting a payload.
Endpoint documentation is not write authorization; owner approval remains mandatory.
Order, warehouse, timeout and finance fields are sensitive and store-specific.
Public US SLA guidance requires policy recheck before a commitment.
SFS is selective and is not official full-managed commerce mode.
Eligibility and stacking require authenticated Seller Hub evidence.
Feature names do not prove account access, API coverage or successful use.
Public analytics families and descriptions do not prove authenticated data, fields, export, API, AI or automatic action.
Read access requires matching store authorization and does not authorize payment changes.
Mode/site-specific fields and formulas cannot be generalized.
Category expansion does not prove clothing/home/custom/full-category store types.
Education does not replace live policies, tests or regulatory evidence.
Public onboarding and solution-provider descriptions do not prove an app, store authorization or connector.
Visible solution groups and API names do not establish store authorization or T One execution support.

T One recognizes this official mode but never executes it or exposes it as a private_tenant selectable identity.
The document proves a personalized-customization workflow exists, not a generic customization store type or T One permission to handle customer customization data.
Tool descriptions and test data exist, but each tool required login and no request or publish was executed.
Public account-type eligibility does not select or qualify private_tenant's developer identity; qualification is owner-controlled and durable.
The store main account must authorize; temporary authorization material and store secrets must never enter task payloads.
Domains and required header schemas do not provide credentials, authorization, rate limits or a successful call.
One application serves one type; POP and SHEIN self-run visibility does not make them executable T One modes. Conflicting semi-managed stock descriptions require live-store resolution.
Internal image-recognition, screening and human-review controls are not seller APIs or execution permissions.
Program-level performance insights and market announcements do not prove a store's enabled sites, model fields or authorization.
A listed partner or AI claim is not platform-native capability, installed software, authorization or verified data scope.
Selection-dependent linked rules supplement the base template. No signed call, store/category authorization or connector was proven; full-managed remains recognition-only.
Only published/approved SPUs are queryable. Inventory and attribute order are explicitly absent; POP is not mapped to a supported T One mode and no store call occurred.

The public query schema separates total, locks, usable, transit and per-warehouse inventory and documents a dated invType migration. No signed store read, live quantity, update permission, lock mutation or connector was proven; unsupported modes remain recognition-only.

Per-item idempotency and failedList inspection are required; protected order inventory and SHEIN physical warehouse stock are not generic mutation targets. No signed write, permission or connector was proven.
The current event page does not list semi-managed. An event schema is not a subscription, callback receiver or live inventory value.
The event is a trigger/key, not complete order truth or permission to fulfill, refund or alter payment.
The event is not return detail, refund authority or external-message permission.
List polling is a signed store-scoped read with bounded time, pagination and dedup requirements; it is not detail, sign or refund authority.
Current detail separates return, logistics, receipt, per-goods evidence and mode-specific costs, but remains a read surface and public examples are not tenant facts.
The solution establishes list/notice-detail-delivery-sign sequencing and a store-level limit. Sign and refund remain owner-gated, and auto-sign timing varies by country.
Public callback/signature/acknowledgement guidance does not prove a configured receiver. Resolve the documented header/body-format inconsistency only in the official test environment.
One non-order retry and two order-event retries are not a complete delivery guarantee or substitute for durable idempotent processing.
